items.detail: A snapshot records each repository of the instance's GitHub owners with its open pull requests and the latest runs on main, read with gh.
items.label: GitHub repositories, pull requests and CI

items.detail: A repository with a checkout is recorded with its local state, its latest release and its planning store.
items.label: Local checkout state

items.detail: Each live agent session is recorded with the repository its working directory lies in.
items.label: Live sessions

items.detail: The open blocker artifacts each repository's planning store holds on origin/main are recorded after a fetch.
items.label: Blockers

items.detail: Each repository's specification is read on origin/main, one per repository, archived ones left out.
items.label: Specifications

items.detail: A snapshot records the releases and merged pull requests of its window.
items.label: Releases and merged pull requests

items.detail: When the instance names a catalog, each recorded repository says whether the catalog lists it.
items.label: Catalog membership

items.detail: A source that does not answer fails the snapshot and keeps what was already recorded.
items.label: A silent source fails the snapshot

items.detail: Each observation kind a snapshot records is answered by its view.
items.label: Every observation reads back

items.detail: A view on a missing store exits 1 and creates nothing.
items.label: Views create nothing

items.detail: store migrate moves an older store into the tree store, and every view answers as before.
items.label: Store migration

items.detail: Only the observations of the newest complete snapshots are kept, 12 unless the instance says otherwise.
items.label: Observation retention

items.detail: repository shipped lists each release with what merged before it, and the rest as not released.
items.label: Release digest

items.detail: A mark overrides the activity computed from the newest complete snapshot.
items.label: Repository activity and marks

items.detail: A goal is proposed, confirmed and met, and a goal confirmed twice is refused.
items.label: Goals

items.detail: Build slots and other resources are requested, granted, released and refused through one ledger.
items.label: Resource ledger

items.detail: One controller runs per repository, through pause, resume, charter revision and stop.
items.label: Controller records

items.detail: A decision request is escalated to the operator and answered.
items.label: Requests, escalation and answers

items.detail: A class-O decision recorded as conductor's is refused and nothing is kept.
items.label: Decision authority

items.detail: Decision ids are allocated per UTC date, and concurrent records get distinct ones.
items.label: Decision ids

items.detail: A dispatch moves from sent through started, blocked and done, and another is cancelled.
items.label: Dispatch lifecycle

items.detail: Dispatch ids are allocated per UTC day, and a hand-given id that exists is refused.
items.label: Dispatch ids

items.detail: Each first-line message format is parsed into its kind.
items.label: Message formats

items.detail: A message whose first line names no format is rejected with the format, not acted on.
items.label: A message that does not parse is answered with the format

items.detail: A controller writes in its own checkout and its managed worktrees, and nowhere else.
items.label: Controller write boundary

items.detail: A controller messages conductor and the agents it started, and no one else.
items.label: Message boundary

items.detail: A controller reads GitHub and makes no write there.
items.label: No GitHub writes from a controller

items.detail: The hook denies with exit 2, allows with exit 0, and records each denial.
items.label: The hook and its record

items.detail: An allowed tool call is answered with exit 0 without opening the store.
items.label: An allowance never opens the store

items.detail: The controller settings file wires the guard on the five tools it checks.
items.label: Settings wire the guard

items.detail: A session gone from the session list is reported, and a start is not.
items.label: Session exits

items.detail: A fresh rate limit is reported once a day, with a notification.
items.label: Rate limits

items.detail: Conductor's context above the hand-over threshold is reported once per session.
items.label: Context threshold

items.detail: Main's CI turning red, and green again, is reported on a CI pass.
items.label: Main CI

items.detail: Free disk under the low threshold is reported, and reported again only after it has recovered past the clear threshold.
items.label: Free disk

items.detail: The dashboard's data holds one row per session under the checkouts root, with its dispatch.
items.label: Session table

items.detail: Every request reads the sources afresh and writes nothing.
items.label: Read-only

items.detail: The disk panel lists the reclaimable rows largest first, with their total.
items.label: Disk waste

items.detail: The dashboard listens on a free port of 127.0.0.1 and prints its address first.
items.label: Loopback only

items.detail: config validate refuses an unknown key, naming its YAML path.
items.label: Problems named by YAML path

items.detail: config show prints the effective instance after defaults, with every path absolute.
items.label: Effective config

items.detail: Without a config file, config validate says the built-in defaults apply.
items.label: Built-in instance

items.detail: A file's default selects the instance, and the instance setting beats it.
items.label: Several instances

items.detail: A local source lists repositories one or two levels deep and places their sessions.
items.label: Local sources, grouped repositories

items.detail: resource usage counts each message once per repository and session.
items.label: Token usage per repository

items.detail: Every output format prints the same rows and nothing from the conversations.
items.label: Nothing private printed

items.detail: No file of the product names an organization; an organization is a config file.
items.label: No organization in the product

items.detail: The clap command tree is compared with the specification's command block on every test run.
items.label: The command line is the specification's

items.detail: A snapshot reads the operator's Codex thread goals, read-only.
items.label: Codex thread goals

items.detail: Which repository depends on which, read from their manifests rather than declared.
items.label: Dependency map

items.detail: The store's append-cost test holds on a busy machine instead of failing the gate.
items.label: Append-cost test on a loaded host

items.detail: snapshot publish-board writes STATUS.md from the newest complete snapshot.
items.label: Status board

items.detail: The board says what the organization is working on, one line per goal.
items.label: Focus per goal

items.detail: start-controller starts the controller's session, not only its record.
items.label: Starting a controller launches its session

items.detail: A controller profile for Codex sessions, beside the Claude one.
items.label: Codex controller profile

items.detail: A controller's start-of-session reading shrinks, so it reaches its hand-over later.
items.label: A controller starts on less reading

items.detail: A decision records the goal it serves and the value or principle it rests on.
items.label: A decision names its goal and value

items.detail: Messages between sessions travel as files, so sessions of different harnesses reach each other.
items.label: Harness-neutral mailbox

items.detail: The restart message, the ready report and the conductor-dev actor are in the specification.
items.label: Restart and ready messages

items.detail: Every tool call reaches the guard, and a tool it does not know is denied.
items.label: Every tool call is guarded

items.detail: Shell writes are bounded by the harness sandbox rather than by parsing commands.
items.label: Bash writes bounded by the sandbox

items.detail: When the guard cannot record its verdict in time it says so, rather than deny the tool call.
items.label: A store timeout is not a denial

items.detail: A relative cd into another managed tree of the same repository is not taken for another repository.
items.label: Sibling trees of one repository

items.detail: The watch's free-disk reading agrees with df on the same filesystem.
items.label: Free-disk reading matches df

items.detail: The watch reports the largest managed trees by size.
items.label: Largest managed trees

items.detail: Each key config validate accepts is read by a command, the watch or a profile.
items.label: Every config key has an effect

items.detail: The specification's conformance suite runs against the conductor binary.
items.label: Conformance suite against the CLI

source: conductor-docs, from its capability list; every shipped item names the test that holds it
